title: vw, vh, vmin, vmax
learningObjectives: Explain vw, vh, vmin, vmax and choose suitable CSS values for a responsive layout.

understand.concept: Viewport units relate a length to the dimensions of the viewport. vw is based on viewport width, vh on viewport height, vmin on the smaller viewport dimension, and vmax on the larger one. Newer viewport variants such as svh, lvh, and dvh address changing mobile browser UI.
understand.whyItMatters: Viewport units are useful for fluid sizing but can create awkward results when content is forced to fit the screen. Consider mobile browser chrome, zoom, and content that needs more space than the viewport.
understand.analogy: Viewport units use the visible browsing area as a measuring reference rather than the parent element.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the idea; actual sizing follows CSS value resolution and layout algorithms.

explain.narrative: The section's minimum height and padding respond to viewport dimensions. Resize the browser and observe the changes.

examples.explanation: The section's minimum height and padding respond to viewport dimensions. Resize the browser and observe the changes.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered example showing the relevant CSS unit or math function.

practise.guidedTask: Create a responsive hero using vw and vh, then compare vmin and vmax on a tall narrow viewport.
practise.independentTask: Create a small responsive component using the concept. Test narrow and wide viewports, long text, and browser zoom.
hints: Inspect computed values in developer tools.
Change one unit at a time.
Avoid fixed dimensions that unnecessarily clip content.

questions.prompt: Which unit uses the smaller of viewport width and height?
options: A universal unit that always means pixels
questions.explanation: vmin is based on the smaller viewport dimension.

questions.prompt: How should you choose a CSS unit?
options: Match the unit to the desired sizing relationship
Always use px for every property

questions.explanation: The unit's reference and responsive behaviour should match the design requirement.
